en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having the most perfect cone shape among all volcanoes in the world.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic to the dense tropical forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Pacific Ocean.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique freshwater lake situated inside a large volcanic crater on Volcano Island.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its pristine coral atolls.
Batanes is the smallest and northernmost province of the Philippines, famous for its traditional stone houses and rolling hills.
The Philippines holds massive nickel reserves, with major mining operations located in the provinces of Surigao del Norte and Palawan.
Samar is the third-largest island in the Philippine archipelago and is separated from Leyte by the San Juanico Strait.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over two thousand years ago.
The Philippine tarsier is one of the smallest primates in the world, native to the islands of Bohol and Samar.
